name: Pierce County Tourism Promotion Area (TPA) Grant Program
award: No per-award range published; 2027 pool $1,021,450 total (Event Marketing $42,950, Sports Event Marketing $55,500, Conventions $67,500, Leisure Marketing $55,500, Personnel/Admin $800,000)

notes: Funds tourism marketing that produces hotel room nights at Pierce County hotels with 40+ rooms; sub-applications for Event Marketing (300 room nights on peak or 500 total), Sports Event Marketing (200+ room nights per event), Conventions, and Leisure Marketing. Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) or 501(c)(6) at least one year old whose primary mission is year-round countywide tourism promotion, which excludes most single-event producers and all for-profits. A required one-on-one meeting with staff precedes submission through the Grants Management portal; funding is reimbursement-based. Pattern: opens early June, due early July for the following calendar year.

name: Snohomish County Tourism Promotion Area (TPA) Grant

notes: Funded by a per-room-night charge on county lodging; supports events and marketing that generate overnight stays in Snohomish County, with special consideration for off-season (Jan to May, Sep to Dec). Apply at least 4 months before the event for requests under $50,000 and 6 months before for larger requests; the board votes at its monthly meeting (third Tuesday, Zoom) and applicants are encouraged to present. Funding is annual (reapply each calendar year), reimbursement-based with proof of payment, and final reports are due Dec 31 of the project year. Eligibility of applicant type is not restricted on the page; confirm for-profit eligibility with staff.

Final report with budget, attendance and photos due within 45 days after the event; missing it disqualifies future funding. Pattern: applications Nov 1 to 30, decisions in January.

name: City of Spokane Tourism and Cultural Investment (TACI) Grant

Events must be within Spokane city limits, free and open to the public (registration fees allowed), not primarily fundraisers, and the applicant needs a City business license and liability insurance. Reimbursement only, with advance payment available in limited cases; post-event evaluation due within 90 days. Pattern: opens March 1, due March 31, awards late April, for events in the fiscal year starting July 1.

name: Bellevue Festivals & Events Incubator Program
funder: Visit Bellevue / Bellevue Tourism Promotion Area / City of Bellevue
opens: Ongoing; decisions once per quarter, 90 to 120 days after application
notes: Cash grants paid 60% up front (four months before the event) and 40% after the final report, so this is not a reimbursement program. Favors multi-day events that fill Bellevue hotels on weekend nights, draw out-of-region visitors, fall in Jan to Apr or Nov to Dec, and fit focus areas (technology, wellness, culinary, multicultural, shopping, creative economy). Recipients display the Visit Bellevue logo, promote Visit Bellevue hotel room blocks, collect attendee data and complete an economic impact report. Awards follow a three-year funding cycle for growing events. Applicant type is not restricted.

name: City of Wenatchee Tourism Promotion Area (TPA) Funds
funder: City of Wenatchee TPA Board (joint with Lodging Tax Advisory Committee)
award: Recent requests $3,510 to $25,000; 2026 TPA budget $45,000 (LTAC budget $100,000 separate)

notes: Wenatchee's $2 per room night TPA fee funds a small tourism events pool administered alongside the city's lodging tax grants and reviewed at monthly joint meetings. Applicants indicate nonprofit status, hold a city business license, sign a municipal services contract with insurance naming the City, use the approved Wenatchee logo, and file a post-event economic impact report (attendance, travel distance, overnight stays). Reimbursement only after costs are incurred. Funds tend to run out mid-year (the 2026 tracker showed about $25,000 TPA remaining in June), so apply early in the calendar year.

name: Port of Walla Walla Tourism Fund

Staff review, then the Port Commission approves at a regular meeting and notifies the applicant. Applicant type is not restricted on the page. Submit the fillable PDF application and acknowledge the Port Tourism Policy.

notes: Four categories: Neighborhood & Community, City Artist, Educational and Cultural focus; projects must serve Sammamish residents, take place in the city, and be delivered within 12 months (2027 cycle Jan 1 to Dec 17, 2027, funds disbursed Mar 22 to Dec 1). Organizations, individuals, youth, schools and PTSAs may apply; a 70% score threshold applies. Email application materials to the coordinator by the deadline.

name: Shoreline Love Your Community Grant
opens: Rolling while funds last; apply 4 to 6 weeks before the event
notes: Micro-grants for Shoreline residents acting through community, cultural, senior, youth, faith or multifamily-building groups to run cultural events, art projects, trainings and gatherings inside Shoreline. Projects must be completed within two months of approval and documented with receipts and a short report. Recognized neighborhood associations use the separate Neighborhood Mini-Grant instead.

name: Kent Community Arts Support Program

geography.region: Kent and Kent School District service area

notes: Annual support for arts organizations, community groups and independent artists producing performances, exhibits, events and educational programs for Kent residents; nonprofit status encouraged but not required. One application per year. Pattern: due mid-October for the following calendar year.

name: Kent Give Me Culture Grants
award: Up to $1,000
opens: Year-round; apply at least 3 months before the project start
notes: Small flexible grants for arts and culture projects and events serving the Kent public, especially ethnically diverse or underserved communities. Reviewed as received.

name: Renton Municipal Arts Commission Grants
funder: City of Renton Municipal Arts Commission
award: Not published

notes: Quarterly grants for individuals, organizations and community groups producing accessible arts and culture projects and events in Renton, with emphasis on projects bridging cultural gaps for underserved groups. Applications are submitted electronically by 4:30 p.m. on each deadline; details are in the current Grant Guidelines PDF.

name: Federal Way Arts Commission Grant (FY2027)
funder: City of Federal Way Arts Commission
award: Not published

notes: Contract-for-services funding for 501(c)(3) organizations (and individuals with 501(c)(3) status) delivering arts, events and cultural heritage activities in Federal Way between Jan 1 and Dec 31, 2027. Excludes tuition, travel, school activities, administrative costs and salaries. Reimbursed after events with an event report; final invoices due Dec 20, 2027. Pattern: opens mid-July, due late August.

name: Auburn Postmark Arts & Cultural Programming Grant
funder: City of Auburn Parks, Arts & Recreation
award: Typically $500 to $2,000 per project
opens: Posted on Auburn's calls-to-artists page; 2024 cycle documented, current dates not confirmed
notes: Funds free, public arts and cultural programming held at Auburn's Postmark Center for the Arts, proposed by artists, cultural groups, neighborhood or business organizations. Auburn also runs an Artist Project Support Grant for individual artists. Check the city's opportunities page for the current call.

name: Everett Cultural Arts Grants
funder: City of Everett / Everett Cultural Arts Commission

notes: Reimbursement grants for arts projects and events in Everett during the calendar year that are free and open to the public or primarily serve low-income or vulnerable residents. Applicant must be a 501(c)(3), fiscally sponsored by one, or a recognized Everett neighborhood association. The city notes the 2027 application will be released once funding is secured, so confirm before planning.

name: Lynnwood Community Event Collaboration Grant / Event Partnership (in-kind only)
funder: City of Lynnwood Parks, Recreation & Cultural Arts
award: Cash grant suspended for budget reasons; in-kind support only (promotion, staff, facility use, Mayor appearance)

notes: Lynnwood partners with businesses, organizations and nonprofits hosting free public events for 250+ people inside city limits by providing promotion through city channels, facility or space use, staff participation and elected-official appearances. The cash grant component is suspended; no amounts or deadlines apply. For lodging-tax funded Lynnwood tourism grants see the LTAC catalog.

name: Lacey Community and Cultural Events Grant

geography.region: Lacey and Lacey Urban Growth Area

award: $500 to $5,000 reimbursement grants

notes: Pilot program funding free, public, nonprofit-led events in Lacey that build connection and belonging. 501(c)(3) registered in Washington or applying through an eligible fiscal sponsor; one application per organization per cycle; partial awards possible. Funded 2026 events run July 2026 to February 2027.

name: Inspire Olympia Cultural Access Funding (Comprehensive and Impact)
funder: City of Olympia (Inspire Olympia cultural access program)
award: Comprehensive: up to 20% of two-year average income, capped at $85,000 per year for two years; Impact: $5,000 to $50,000
opens: Next cycle dates not published; the first cycle funded 49 organizations
notes: Olympia's voter-approved cultural access sales tax funds Olympia-based nonprofit cultural organizations: Comprehensive (operating support for larger organizations with year-round public and youth programming) and Impact (contracts for services for specific programs, which can include festivals and events). Confirm current cycle and deadlines with the City's Cultural Access Program staff.

funder: City of Port Townsend Arts Commission (PTAC)

award: Not published; Commission sets amounts per project (direct costs only)

notes: Funds direct costs (artist fees, rentals, marketing, production) of performances, exhibits and workshops with artistic merit and public benefit for the Port Townsend/East Jefferson community, or that bring visitors to benefit locals. No capital, operating, hospitality or fundraising-only events. Applications are decided at open public meetings; payment after invoice, W-9 and follow-up report. Check the PTAC page each year for the three deadlines.

name: Inspire Vancouver Cultural Access Grants (Innovation, Impact, Comprehensive)
funder: City of Vancouver (Inspire Vancouver Cultural Access Program)
award: Not published per grant; first-year program budget about $3.85M (typical annual budget about $7M)

Innovation, Impact and Comprehensive tracks mirror Tacoma Creates and Inspire Olympia; awards announced in October with funding in November. Festivals and events run by eligible nonprofits fit the Impact track.

name: Vancouver Culture, Arts and Heritage Grants
funder: City of Vancouver Parks, Recreation and Cultural Services
opens: No dates posted; last documented cycle funded projects July 2024 through December 2025
notes: Reimbursement grants for community arts, culture and heritage projects in Vancouver judged on artistic quality and innovation; individual artists are matched with a sponsoring organization on request. Recent highlight: Vancouver Ballet Folklórico's Día de Muertos celebration. With Inspire Vancouver launching in 2026, confirm whether this program continues.

notes: Small grants for free community events (block parties, picnics, carnivals, cultural and education events) and projects in Vancouver by nonprofits, neighborhood associations, clubs, PTAs and informal groups; for-profits, schools and governments are ineligible. Pays for supplies, rentals, insurance, nonalcoholic food and professional services; not admission-charging events. Impact report due within 30 days.
